claim: Flavell: metacognitive knowledge is mostly about interactions among person, task and strategy variables, not separate stores. This is the seed of a class-by-operator record.
agent_test: Compare operator choice keyed on (task class x operator) against choice keyed on task class alone, equal tokens.

claim: Flavell warned knowledge can be wrong, not activated, activated but ignored, or used but unhelpful; LLM studies show the same breaks (wrong self-knowledge: c18, b21; known but not acted on: a21, a23).
agent_test: Log the four failure types separately when the class record is used; count each.

claim: The three-way declarative/procedural/conditional split is not recovered empirically in human inventories. Two factors (knowledge, regulation) fit; the higher-order three-type model fits badly (CFI .84, RMSEA .11, N=528).
agent_test: Not testable on the agent. Use the terms as design vocabulary, not as claimed separate modules.

claim: Young children say they are ready or understand without a check and are wrong; a self-feeling needs an outside check.
agent_test: Compare the agent's self-reported done against a code-side check at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs follow a named strategy well (procedural knowledge is easy) but do not choose better than a fixed strategy when left free (conditional knowledge is weak): Phi-4 free 47.2 percent vs forced 45.1 to 49.0; GPT-3.5 MRP 0.433 vs best fixed SPP 0.469. Select-then-Solve adds: zero-shot self-routing averaged 46.7 vs Direct 47.6 across 4 models (GPT-5 tied, Qwen3-Max worse, 42.4 vs 49.8).
agent_test: Run model-side operator choice vs best fixed operator vs random operator at equal tokens, per class.

claim: An oracle that picks the best strategy per problem has large headroom on some tasks (Phi-4 TruthQuest 82.9 vs 47.2; R1-Distill 90.1 vs 63.4) and small headroom on others (ZebraLogic 37.7 vs 27.3; 36.4 vs 32.0). Second source: Select-then-Solve per-item oracle beats best fixed paradigm by 12.4 to 24.1 points on 4 models and 10 benchmarks (optimistic: max over noisy runs).
agent_test: Measure the per-class oracle gap on our items before building the record; skip classes with small gap.

claim: Code-side combination (majority vote, verifier) beats any single strategy but stays far below the oracle (54.9 to 57.3 vs 82.9 on Phi-4 TruthQuest). Learned routers recover only about 26 percent of the oracle gap (Select-then-Solve, 229 test tasks).
agent_test: Test vote across operators vs best single operator at equal tokens.

claim: A strong model can build a skill catalogue once (22 skills GSM8K, 117 MATH) and skill-matched exemplars beat topic-matched, random-from-pool and complex-CoT exemplars (MATH GPT-4: 53.88 vs 50.31, 50.30, CoT 42.2).
agent_test: Replicate on our tasks: skill-matched vs topic-matched vs random hints at equal tokens. One paper, one run, no CIs.

claim: The catalogue built by a strong model transfers to a weaker model (Mixtral) and other datasets, but weak models cannot build it (Llama-2 70B; Mixtral clusters everything together).
agent_test: Build the record with the strongest model once; use it for cheaper calls.

claim: Gains from skill or strategy selection shrink as baseline accuracy rises (GSM8K GPT-4 93.0 to 94.3; SMART +15.2 down to +3.5 across models; MC2 small on GSM8K).
agent_test: Gate the record step on baseline pass rate; confirm no gain on easy classes.

claim: Choosing reasoning modules once per task, then following that structure on every instance, beats CoT on structure-heavy tasks (GPT-4 BBH 81 vs 75, T4D 85 vs 52) at 10-40x fewer calls than self-consistency, but only 1 to 7 points on MATH where 74.7 percent of failures are arithmetic.
agent_test: Test per-class structure fixed once vs per-instance choice at equal tokens.

claim: A fixed metacognitive prompt gives modest gains and overthinking errors (68.3 percent of MP errors); forcing a plan-monitor-evaluate cycle on a non-reasoning-trained model hurts GSM8K (69.55 vs 80.71 plain).
agent_test: Compare a fixed metacognitive prompt vs plain at equal tokens per class; keep only if net positive.

claim: LLMs have above-chance domain-level self-knowledge but do not act on it when told: giving own calibration scores left confident failure at 0.605 vs 0.600; external control cut it to 0.143.
agent_test: Put the class record in the prompt vs enforce it by code; compare confident-failure rate.

claim: Self-knowledge is domain-specific and does not compose: transfer index 0.019 to 0.175; compositional calibration error 0.43 to 0.94.
agent_test: Measure the record on mixed-class items; treat mixed items as unknown until measured.

claim: Model confidence used as a control signal helps mainly on low-confidence items (0.16 to 0.42) and not on high ones (0.67 to 0.64), but random retry at matched budget (45.7) lies inside the interval of the full harness (47.0 [37,57]) on 100 items.
agent_test: Always include random retry at matched K as control.

claim: A competence self-assessment is part of the agent gain but not all of it: ALFWorld novel tasks MUSE 84/90, random self-assessment 68/69, lowest-score 59/61, Reflexion 45/51, ReAct 35/35. Most of the gain over ReAct survives random assessment.
agent_test: Ablate the record with random and inverted entries at equal tokens.

claim: Learned or external selectors help: AdaptThink cuts length 53 percent with accuracy +2.4 (always-NoThinking loses 12.7 points); Meta-R1 87.0 vs 84.0 at 31 percent fewer tokens; SOFAI-LM escalation beats the heavy solver alone; SMART RL selection beats fixed strategies.
agent_test: Route easy items to a short path, escalate on impasse; compare with always-long at equal tokens. All but SOFAI-LM train weights.

claim: Accumulating procedural knowledge from the agent's own traces cuts tokens (up to 46 percent) and raises accuracy (MC2 MATH-500 78.93 to 85.13; Game-of-24 41.33 to 88.67), more for weaker backbones.
agent_test: Write the class record from own solved items; test on held-out items of the same class; report order effect.

claim: Model reasoning traces show self-awareness in 19 percent of traces vs 49 percent of human traces, and it is negatively associated with success (NPMI -0.141); guidance helps ill-structured tasks (up to +66.7) and sometimes hurts (down 72).
agent_test: Apply scaffolding by class only; test sign of effect per class.

claim: Users overestimate LLM accuracy with default explanations; matching explanation length to model confidence narrows the gap (N=301).
agent_test: Low priority; tie stated confidence to measured record.

claim: Prompted self-doubt ('could you be wrong?') has only qualitative support, no accuracy numbers.
agent_test: Do not add without a measured test.

claim: No opened study tests conditional knowledge as a factor separate from procedural knowledge, in humans or LLMs. KAPRO separates knowing-whether-a-tool-is-needed from acting (GPT-5 Acc_know 94.22 vs Acc_act 58.54), a partial proxy, but it is not a procedural-vs-conditional ablation.
agent_test: Design a record ablation separating can-run-operator from knows-when-to-pick-it.

claim: Metacognitive strategy instruction in school pupils has positive effects that persist (g about 0.50 post, similar at follow-up), larger in primary school. Values come from search snippets only.
agent_test: Background only, not testable on the agent.

claim: A learned per-task router gives a modest accuracy gain over the best fixed strategy, and a larger cost saving. Select-then-Solve: 53.1 vs 50.3 (4 models, 229 test tasks, 26 percent of oracle gap); RTR: 82.5 vs 80.0 at 1091 vs 2745 tokens; PRISM +3.8 to +9.1 on math.
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare record-based routing vs best fixed operator vs random operator on our own classes, 3+ repeats.

claim: Random strategy choice loses to the best single model by about 10 points (RTR: 69.5 vs 80.0 ID; 79.0 vs 93.7 unseen), so a routing gain over random is not evidence of a gain over the best fixed choice.
agent_test: Always report three arms: random operator, best fixed operator, record-based.

claim: Choice made in code from measured data beats choice made by the model from a prompt on the same items: Select-then-Solve router 53.1 vs self-route 46.7; Semantic Router (code gating) +10.24 pp and -48.5 percent tokens. Confounded with what information each had, so not a clean prompt-vs-code test.
agent_test: Run record-in-prompt vs record-in-code with the same record content.

claim: Models know a tool or step is unneeded yet do it anyway: KAPRO Kc/Aw 1.76 to 45.48 percent across 18 models; r = -0.748 between knowing score and tool calls. Reasoning models are not safer (Sonnet 4.5 think 41.96 vs instruct 23.12).
agent_test: Log 'known and not applied' separately from 'wrong' and 'not retrieved'.

claim: Self-selection works only at frontier strength and then mostly ties: GPT-5 self-route 60.3 equals Direct 60.3; weaker models fall below or at Direct. No threshold has been measured for our model.
agent_test: Measure our model's self-route accuracy vs Direct on 3 task classes before relying on self-selection.

claim: Cold-start and minimum-sample question is open: Select-then-Solve trained on 300 to 400 labelled items per model; RTR on about 1470 (derived); Bandits in Prod uses 10-arm warm-up and sqrt(t) arm growth. No study gives items per class at which a measured record beats a prior.
agent_test: Plot accuracy of choice vs items seen per class (5, 10, 20, 40).

claim: Learned self-knowledge decays with distance from its training domain: consistency tracking grows with distance (r=0.49); accuracy tracking holds only locally. Task-side transfer of a router to easy unseen sets works (RTR 93.1 to 95.3) but mixed-class and cross-model transfer are untested.
agent_test: Test the record on mixed-class items and on a cheaper model.

claim: Primary human sources (Schraw and Dennison 1994, Schraw and Moshman 1995, Paris 1983, Flavell 1970s studies) were not opened; exact N and recall figures remain unknown.
agent_test: Obtain by library copy.
